newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply off, pummelled by rate woes.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply off, pummelled by rate woes.

text.p: Concerns about higher interest rates continued to pummel Hong Kong stocks on Thursday and the Hang Seng Index closed with heavy losses as investors awaited next Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting.
The index slid 179.09 points, or 1.42 percent, to 12,472.33.
Turnover was HK$9.28 billion compared with HK$8.12 billion on Wednesday.
"Right now the market is very much dictated by the direction of interest rates," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International
He said investors were nervously watching the U.S. long bond, which fell 10/32 on Wednesday to yield 6.99 percent.
Analysts said Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan was also scheduled to testify later on Thursday before the Joint Economic Committee, which had heightened nervous sentiment.
The blue-chip index has lost 264.20 points, or 2.07 percent, so far this week.
"It seems not to be reacting to positive news on the earnings front," said Pauline Gately, regional strategist at Merrill Lynch.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd beat market expectations on Wednesday when it announced a 33 percent rise in interim net profit to HK$5.32 billion.
The stock closed HK$1.25 lower at HK$63.50.
"Volume in most of the blue chips is still low despite the fact that they reported excellent earnings," said Tang.
Hang Lung Development Co Ltd and Amoy Properties Ltd also released interim results on Thursday.
Hang Lung posted net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996, of HK$1.44 billion compared with HK$1.07 billion. Its shares fell HK$0.25 to HK$14.00.
Its Amoy Properties unit reported interim net profit of HK$959.7 million compared with HK$836.6 million. The stock fell HK$0.30 to HK$8.20.

Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd reported its first final results on Thursday, posting proforma combined net profit of HK$360.42 million -- beating its own forecast contained in its initial public offering prospectus of not less than HK$310 million.
The stock fell HK$1.80 to HK$33.70 after rising HK$2.40 on Wednesday.
Analysts said the market could remain sluggish ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25.
"It would appear that there is some real caution ahead of the FOMC," said Gately.
